27 A pipe, closed at one end, has a loudspeaker at the open end. For some frequencies of sound
from the loudspeaker, a stationary sound wave is formed in the air within the pipe with an
antinode at the open end of the pipe.
0.85 m
loudspeaker
pipe
The length of the pipe is 0.85 m.
The speed of sound in air is 340 m s–1.
Which frequency of sound from the loudspeaker would not produce a stationary wave?
A
100 Hz
B
200 Hz
C
300 Hz
D
500 Hz

hints: Notice the pipe is $0.85 \text{ m}$ long with a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end by the loudspeaker.
Recall that a closed pipe fits only odd quarters of a wavelength: $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4$ and so on.
Calculate the lowest resonant frequency from $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and check which listed frequency in Hz is not an odd multiple of it.
walkthrough: The closed end must be a displacement node and the open end a displacement antinode, as stated for the $0.85 \text{ m}$ pipe.
This gives the resonance condition $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$ for $n = 1, 2, 3...$, so only odd numbers of quarter wavelengths fit.
Using $v = f\lambda$, the allowed frequencies are $f = (2n-1)v/(4L)$.

Higher resonances are odd multiples: $300 \text{ Hz}$, $500 \text{ Hz}$, $700 \text{ Hz}$ and so on, while $200 \text{ Hz}$ is an even $2 \times 100 \text{ Hz}$ multiple and cannot satisfy the node-antinode condition.
Therefore $200 \text{ Hz}$ would not produce a stationary wave. This is option B

A.explanation: 100 Hz is the fundamental frequency with $L = \lambda/4$, so it does form a stationary wave.

B.explanation: 200 Hz is $2 \times 100$ Hz, an even multiple, which cannot fit a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end.

C.explanation: 300 Hz is $3 \times 100$ Hz, the third harmonic with $L = 3\lambda/4$, so it does form a stationary wave.

D.explanation: 500 Hz is $5 \times 100$ Hz, the fifth harmonic with $L = 5\lambda/4$, so it does form a stationary wave.
